title: Product decomposition of derivative influence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $J$ be any subset of its coordinates, and let $i$ be any coordinate. If the cube is sampled by choosing signs independently and uniformly on $J$ and on its complement, then the expected squared discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ equals the influence of $f$ at $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is any real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is any finite set of coordinates in the cube
$i$ is any coordinate in the cube
